title: Identification of the affine structural mate by composite counits
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, and $1\le m\le n$. Set $A=\mathcal O_E/(\varpi^n)$, $B=\mathcal O_E/(\varpi^m)$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. For a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $Y$ [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], write $a_Y:Y\to s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $F_{Y,R}=Ra_{Y,R!}\dashv G_{Y,R}=a_{Y,R}^{\times}$, $\omega_{Y,R}=G_{Y,R}R_s$, and $\varepsilon_{Y,R}:F_{Y,R}\omega_{Y,R}\to R_s$, for $R=A,B$, on ordinary small etale module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-amb-etale-compact-support, thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. Let $T_Y=-\otimes_A^LB$ [def-kun-derived-tensor], and denote the canonical compact-support coefficient comparison by $c_{Y,K}:T_sF_{Y,A}K\to F_{Y,B}T_YK$ [lem-fix-compact-support-coefficient-change]. Here bounded constructible finite-Tor means constructible cohomology, zero outside a finite interval, and integers $a\le b$ such that tensoring with every degree-zero module sheaf has cohomology only in $[a,b]$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes, def-kun-tor-amplitude]. Assume the named dualizing objects are bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude. Define $u_Y:T_Y\omega_{Y,A}\to\omega_{Y,B}$ to be the unique map with $\varepsilon_{Y,B}F_{Y,B}(u_Y)=(T_s\varepsilon_{Y,A})c_{Y,\omega_{Y,A}}^{-1}$, using $T_sA_s\cong B_s$. Let $i:Y\hookrightarrow P=\mathbf A^r_k$ be closed with $Y$ affine. Let $I_R=Ri^!_{\mathrm{et},R}$ have closed exceptional counit $e_{R,H}:i_{R*}I_RH\to H$, and use the counit-compatible identifications $\omega_{Y,R}\cong I_R\omega_{P,R}$ [lem-exc-closed-ambient, def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Suppose $u_P$ is invertible and the closed comparison $b^e_{i,M}:T_YI_AM\cong I_BT_PM$, $M=\omega_{P,A}$, obeys $e_{B,T_PM}i_*b^e_{i,M}=(T_Pe_{A,M})c_{i,I_AM}^{-1}$ with the canonical direct-image coefficient map [lem-coef-finite-direct-image]. Then, under those structural identifications,
$$u_Y=I_B(u_P)\circ b^e_{i,M}.$$
In particular $u_Y$ is invertible. The equality concerns the actual counit-defined maps: with $v=I_B(u_P)b^e_{i,M}$, $F_R=F_{P,R}$ and the normalized compact-support composition $c_Y=F_B(c_{i,I_AM})c_{P,i_*I_AM}$, their transposes satisfy $(\varepsilon_{Y,B}F_{Y,B}v)c_Y=T_s\varepsilon_{Y,A}$. Only coefficient components at the independently finite-Tor objects $I_AM$ and $M$ are inverted; no finite-Tor claim on $i_*I_AM$ is required for an inverse in this calculation.

proof.text: The proper/open compact-support coefficient map is invertible on every input over these Noetherian schemes. Thus t and h are invertible, and cY, which is defined as h followed by F_B(d), is invertible. This stronger result is valid even though no finite-Tor hypothesis was given for i_*N.

proof.text: Expand the composite counit with Adjunction.comp_counit_app. Naturality of the closed B-counit at uP moves I_B(uP) through that counit. Substitute the given equation for b, use functoriality, and cancel d followed by its inverse.

proof.text: Use compactScalarMap, the actual natural transformation with components compactSupportMap, at the closed A-counit i_*N to M. Its naturality moves the forward h across that counit. The assumed equation for uP and cancellation of t against its inverse give cY followed by F_Y,B(b followed by I_B(uP)) followed by epsY,B equals T_S(epsY,A) followed by the scalar unit.

proof.text: Cancel cY in the preceding equation and apply injectivity of the inverse composite-adjunction Hom equivalence. Its inverse is F_Y,B(-) followed by epsY,B, so the resulting equality is exactly the stipulated uY = b followed by I_B(uP). Both factors are isomorphisms by hypothesis and preservation of isomorphisms by IB. Transport this instance across the equality. The retained equation gives the final conjunct.
